config.winner_rule: Written before the run. The adapter is chosen only if, on the dev cases of `scenarios`, the interval of its grounded_rate minus the prompted version's lies wholly above zero, and its unsupported_claim_rate, schema_valid_rate, abstain_when_insufficient and answer_when_answerable are each no worse than the prompted version's. Otherwise the prompted version stays in the product and the record says the tuning did not beat it.
config.winner_reason: the adapter's grounded_rate is not shown above the prompted version's

max_gold_choice.rule: the smallest value reaching 300 usable examples that fits the 7 GB cap; if none reaches 300, the highest tested that fits. The honesty rule is unchanged: a card cites every gold turn, an example with more gold turns than MAX_GOLD is dropped, never shortened. 25% abstained cap, seed 13, no new invented data.
max_gold_choice.citation_limit_in_schema: none: Finding.evidence is an unbounded list
max_gold_choice.estimate_not_measured: Superseded by MEMORY_CHOICE: the 2048 cap measured 9.70 GB on the first probe, not under 7 GB.
max_gold_choice.note: No value reaches 300. The probe trains on the first rows, not the longest, so its peak memory may understate the run's.

memory_choice.problem: the first probe at MAX_LEN 2048, batch 2, full logits peaked at 9.70 GB, over the 7.0 GB limit
memory_choice.chosen: MAX_LEN 917 with both savers (micro-batch 1 with gradients added over the 2 rows of a step; loss from the card's tokens only) and the limit lowered from 7.0 to 5.5 GB: a 3.5-hour training run at 1408 was stopped, because the card really has about 5.7 GB free (Windows holds about 2 GB), so long rows spilled into shared memory. No example is shortened; longer ones are dropped before the 25% abstained cap. NaN guard unchanged.

revision.from: MAX_LEN 1408 under a 7.0 GB limit (160 examples)
revision.rule: the largest cap whose worst real row peaks under 5.5 GB. Per-row peaks come from one forward and backward of each of the 212 rows with both savers (tools/e5_memory_diag.py's method), plus 0.24 GB for the optimizer, which the three worst rows measured in full steps added each time.
revision.worst_row_kept: 721 tokens (274 card): 5.18 GB + 0.24 = 5.42 GB; the next row, 918 tokens, is 5.44 + 0.24 = 5.68 GB
revision.smaller_model_estimate: NOT RUN, an estimate from config.json files only (Qwen3.5-2B: hidden 2048, 24 layers; 0.8B: hidden 1024, 24 layers; same 248k vocabulary; downloads 4.55 GB and 1.75 GB, not in the cache): all 212 rows would stay under 5.5 GB, training about 14 min (2B) or 8 min (0.8B), against 5.5 min for the 82 examples on the 4B. The fit behind it is rough (rms 0.35 GB).

base_model_2b.decision: the person, 2026-11-05: Qwen/Qwen3.5-2B for both sides, all 212 examples, MAX_LEN 2048, limit 5.5 GB kept
base_model_2b.estimate_not_measured: per row from the 4B's measured peaks (weights 3.5 GB to 2.0 GB, the layer part scaled by 2048x24 / 2560x32 = 0.6, the card-logits part unchanged, plus 0.24 GB for the optimizer): worst row 4.75 GB, none over 5.5; the 2B tokenizer gives the same length on all 212 rows. Projected 3.4 to 5.1 s per step of 2 rows, 212 steps = 12 to 18 min. A GPU run must confirm it; check_vram still stops at the first step over 5.5.

memory_choice.tool: tools/e5_memory_diag.py (synthetic rows of an exact length built from real ones, inside the tool only)
memory_choice.reading: The card's length matters as much as the input's (logits of the card span), so a cap on total tokens is the only knob: the synthetic table is not a bound. The table is from the first 7.0 GB limit; see revision.
memory_choice.note: Seconds per step jumped to 30 to 85 s in several runs with an allocated peak of 6.9 to 7.2 GB (Windows shared-memory spill, since other use of the 8 GB card and the allocator's reserve sit on top of the allocated peak); not at 5.7 GB.

base_model_change.why: The card has about 5.5 GB of real room (Windows holds about 2 GB). On the 4B that limit keeps 82 examples (MAX_LEN 917); the 2B keeps all 212. The person decided on 2026-11-05 that both sides, the prompted base with the chosen prompt and the adapter, run on the 2B.

config.synthetic_statement: The training mix includes synthetic data: the invented train-only scenario set (datasets/scenarios_train), marked synthetic, besides QMSum train conversations.
config.overlap_guard_statement: Limit of T6.1's overlap guard: it refuses a training scenario at 50% shared 3-word windows with a dev or test conversation. It guards against accidental reuse in our hand-written set, not against a deliberate paraphrase.
config.independent_read_statement: An independent read of the invented train-only set, before training, is what caught real near-copies of held-out scenarios; the 3-word overlap guard scored them only 0.13 to 0.18, so it could not have caught them. Those cases were rewritten and read again.
config.qmsum_statement: QMSum dev cards are judged by Haiku like the rest, on published labels; sending that text to Claude through `claude -p` is approved (docs/HANDOFF.md section 8). Their rows stay in git-ignored files and no raw text is committed; the record holds only the figures, so check_run cannot recompute them.
config.retrieval_note: Retrieval for both sides is the product's (configs/retrieval.json), computed once and shared.

judge.statement: Judge: Haiku through `claude -p`, one claim per call, rubric e2-v1. Haiku failed the written calibration against Sonnet (docs/DECISIONS.md entry 56: agreement 0.813 against the local judge's 0.870, difference -0.057 with an interval wholly below zero). The explanation there, that the local judge says supported to nearly everything and so gains from the base rate, is a reading and not proof. Sonnet did not grade E5. No person reviewed these judgements (no config.judge_review), so they are provisional, not claims.

config.schema_valid_note: schema_valid_rate is the share of cases whose first model reply parsed as a Card, before the retry.
config.decoding: schema-constrained: the card's JSON schema limits every token (llm/json_constrain.py) on both sides, as Ollama's `format` does for E6's models; the first run, unconstrained, is kept under the old folder name
